engine_bytes.rule: The board pins the engine inputs by sha256 (evaluation_engine_inputs and the files named by the engine command). The run executes exactly the pinned bytes: the placeholders resolve to a spellbench checkout at 0c486ed for the adapter files, the pinned python.exe, the pinned catalog and the pinned bridge, never to a checkout of main.
engine_bytes.against_the_2026-11-14_run: Only agent_bridge_v1.exe differs from that run's engine_files (3338b4d8 to f8bae9fd). The adapter files, python.exe and the catalog are byte for byte the same.
engine_bytes.main_differs: Main's kernel_history_v2.py (b41e376a) and kernel_observation_v2.py (3bfc00de) differ from the pinned bytes: spellbench d4dcb42 (grid board, ProjectionError repair) changed them after 0c486ed, and it is the only change to them since. The other seven adapter files on main equal the pinned bytes. The definition on main therefore cites files whose current bytes differ from the recorded hashes, as the earlier pins did.
engine_bytes.audit_bytes: The history two-world audit, check_engine_v2, check_private_preview_v2, the gorge-ar8 smoke, the sweep and the unrated pass ran on the pinned 0c486ed bytes. The adapter pytest and the goldens check ran on main's bytes (see adapter_tests).
engine_bytes.untested: The grid-board ProjectionError class ('known hand facts exceed the hand count', off-mirror Faeries) is untested on the pinned bytes. This ladder plays mirrors only, and none appears in its 2,688 published games or in the unrated runs.

rated_run.games: 15 rung matchups plus 3 entrant matchups of chains-a-c4-u1048576 (Basilisk 2) against g115, oh2-r2s1-b512 and oh2-r2s1-b512-argmax, 18 blocks of 128 games = 2,304 games
rated_run.validity: Strict: every 128-game block needs at least 125 natural endings, and every rung's total across the run needs at least 97% natural endings (forfeits of any cause, halts and truncations all count against). A block below 125 invalidates the run even if its rung total passes.
rated_run.not_in_this_run: oh2-r2s1-b512-s4a-16k-k4 is not scheduled. It stays in the roster and is listed as pending on the board until its own entrant-only re-rate on this evaluation version; its 2.0.0 placement is a record of that version and not a 2.1.0 rating.
rated_run.excluded: Run 2026-11-14 stays excluded and published as a record; runs 2026-11-08 and 2026-11-09 and their snapshots stay published under evaluation 2.0.0.

v4_visibility.what_it_tests: At every decision of neutral private-support games on the eight board decks, the acting seat's V4 boundary and x_kernel_flat_v4 encoding are unchanged when the search sampler redeterminizes every hidden card the engine's knowledge tables mark as unknown to that seat; and every place one player learned hidden cards of the other (library look or reveal, hand reveal, library reorder revealed to the opponent) is a reviewed site marked in the source. It is a consistency check against the engine's own knowledge tables plus a pinned enumeration of reveal sites, not a proof against a fact the tables wrongly mark as known.
v4_visibility.same_sites_as_89fb69a95: the same 14 calls at the same lines as the 4fccd3ebc receipt (the repair is in push_paid_activation, after the last reveal site); same 16 games, 4,731 decisions, 14,193 sampled worlds
v4_visibility.coverage: The audit exercised 6 of the 25 marked library-reveal calls and 8 of the 36 marked hand-reveal calls. The 21 and 35 present at 89fb69a95 rest on the static enumeration reviewed in mtg-kernel #462 and #476; the 4 library and 1 hand marked calls added since are premodern card code from mtg-kernel #465 and #467, outside this board's pool. No library reorder call is marked as revealing to the opponent.

paid_ninjutsu_repair.tool: cargo test --release -p mtg-kernel --lib paid_ninjutsu_keeps_the_waiting_hand_source_pristine_for_opponent_infoset, and integrations/mtg_kernel bridge transcript equality
paid_ninjutsu_repair.regression_test: fails on the test-only commit aaab89a8a ("Ninja of the Deep Hours in seat PlayerId(0): I1 hidden object 0 is not pristine") and passes on d11d986d9
paid_ninjutsu_repair.transcript_equality: old (3338b4d8) and new bridge answer byte for byte on 24 games (8 decks x 3 seeds) in plain and in --x-kernel-flat-v4 --private-v2-support mode
paid_ninjutsu_repair.halt_attribution: All 11 published halts (rated run 2026-11-08 games 1567, 1678, 1711, 1743, 1823; rated run 2026-11-09 game 350; run 2026-11-14 games 14, 30, 46, 47, 222) are paid ninjutsu activations of Ninja of the Deep Hours or Moon-Circuit Hacker from hand, followed by the returned attacker and the halt at the next export. Replayed on the old bridge (3338b4d8) all 11 halt again with every ledger field equal to the published row; replayed on the new bridge all 11 end natural. A halt for another reason is not seen in any published or unrated game, but the exporter still refuses any untracked hidden object with a non-default field, so a state not yet met could halt again.
paid_ninjutsu_repair.halted_games_replayed: diagnostic only: bench rerun refuses a changed bridge, so the recorded config and secret were replayed directly
paid_ninjutsu_repair.scripted_ninjutsu: 72 scripted human-seat Faeries games against chains-a-c4-u1048576 playing Burn: 72 natural, 0 halted, 21 ninjutsu activations in 19 games (the same script had 13 of 17 ninjutsu games halt on 4fccd3ebc)
paid_ninjutsu_repair.halt_sweep: unrated Faeries mirrors on this bridge: 647 games between uniform, g115, oh2-r2s1-b512, oh2-r2s1-b512-argmax and chains-a-c4-u1048576, 0 not natural. 560 of them (336 among the four non-anchor bots, every pairing in both seats) ran with a tap wrapper around the adapter that counts ninjutsu activations: 560 natural, 1,416 activations in 451 games. The other 87 ran without the tap. The sweep is the only run that used the wrapper; the unrated pass below ran the board's plain command.
